title.value: Quantum Tensor Networks, Stochastic Processes, and Weighted Automata

title.quote: Quantum Tensor Networks, Stochastic Processes, and Weighted Automata

analysis.description: The paper explores the connections between quantum tensor network models, stochastic processes, and weighted automata. It establishes equivalence results between models from these fields and discusses their expressiveness and applications in probabilistic modeling. By identifying equivalences across these models, the paper facilitates cross-application of methods and results from different disciplines.

type.justification: The paper establishes theoretical connections and equivalence between different models from quantum tensor networks, stochastic processes, and weighted automata. It focuses on theoretical aspects like model expressiveness and relationships.
type.quote: We address this gap by showing how stationary or uniform versions of popular quantum tensor network models have equivalent representations in the stochastic processes and weighted automata literature, in the limit of infinitely long sequences.

name.justification: Matrix Product States (MPS) are discussed as a quantum tensor network model, which is central to the paper.
name.quote: Matrix product states (MPS) were first developed by the physics community as compact representations of often intractable wave functions of complex quantum systems.

is_contributed.quote: Summary of Contributions In Section 2, we demonstrate that uniform Matrix states (uMPS) are equivalent to predictive state representations and stochastic weighted automata.
